analysis:
The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/developer/test.md. At head lines 2115-2131 it adds a test-instructions paragraph for the 'Model Requant Upload' workflow (python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/models). It describes offline checks run with a fake aws and python3: a secret-free preflight, a job in the prod environment, master-only runs, a check of both R2 key sets that prints only pass or fail, an upload gated on this run's check, hash-pinned tools, and a selftest before any secret. The supplied units are unchanged base text from lines 2731-3418, so the changed region is visible only in the patch excerpt. I read that surrounding text and found nothing in it that this PR alters.

No code, configuration, workflow or secret handling changes in the supplied evidence. The text does not weaken any threat-model control. It touches no part of T-041, the prefix cache and SSD tier, or any TB/A asset definition. The description of the check printing only pass or fail, and of tools pinned by hash, is consistent with good secret hygiene, but I cannot verify those properties here. They would live in scripts/models and .github/workflows, which are outside the supplied evidence. Whether the workflow actually enforces the master-only, prod-environment and secret-free-preflight rules stays an unverified contract, not a finding. A reviewer of those files should check it if they change. I identified no concrete security regression, new attack surface or threat-model gap from this documentation-only change.
